summary: Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he studied at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, Dzongsar Shedra, Palyul Chokhorling Monastery, and the University of Virginia. He held posts at Washington University in St. Louis and the University of Nebraska–Lincoln (attested 2011).

An Indologist, he studied at the St. Petersburg University Faculty of Oriental Studies (~1961–1967). His career includes positions at the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1978) and the Faculty of Philosophy at Saint Petersburg State University.

An Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, he studied at the University of Tokyo (~1949–1956) under Kogen Mizuno. He was a professor emeritus at Komazawa University (~1999–2017) and director of the Soto Zen Comprehensive Research Center (attested 2000).

A linguist and Tibetologist, he studied at the University of California, Berkeley (~1973–1978). He held appointments at the Graduate University for Advanced Studies (~1990–2010) and the National Museum of Ethnology, serving as professor (~1989–2010) and professor emeritus (~2010).

Working in Indology and philosophy, he completed his PhD at Hiroshima University under Atsushi Uno, Shoryu Katsura, and Hiroakira Ono. He held teaching posts at Hiroshima Prefectural Chiyoda, Hiroshima Prefectural Kabe, and Takamiya (attested 2005) high schools.

A Buddhist studies scholar, he pursued short-term study under George Baumann at Tübingen University Library. He held posts at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (~1983–1996) and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, serving as deputy director (attested 2012).
A scholar in Buddhist studies, he pursued doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2003–2004). He later held an appointment as a commissioned researcher at Koyasan University (attested 2004).

An Indologist, he studied under Masaaki Hattori (~1963–1969) and earned his PhD from the University of Chicago (~1971–1978). He taught at Kindai University (~1974–1986) and Kyoto University (~1986–2004), where he became professor emeritus (~2004).

Specializing in religious studies and Indology, he studied at Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1967–1971). He held faculty posts at Japan Women's University, Gakushuin Women's College, the University of Tsukuba (~1990–2000), and Kwansei Gakuin University (~2014–2020).

A Buddhist studies and Indology scholar, he earned his BA and PhD at the University of Tokyo and trained at the University of Göttingen. He taught at Rissho University Junior College and the University of Tokyo (1966; 1982–1999).

Working in philosophy and Buddhist studies, he studied at Kyoto University (~1980–1989). He held faculty posts at the Nagoya Institute of Technology (~1994–1998) and Kyoto University as associate professor of philosophy (~2004–2017).
A scholar in Buddhist studies, he held teaching posts at Ryukoku University (attested 1991 as lecturer, 2006 as part-time lecturer) and Shuchiin University (attested 2006 as part-time lecturer).
Specializing in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology, he served as a technical official at the Nara National Museum (~1993–2003) before taking up a post at Kyoto University in ~2003.

An Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, he completed doctoral studies at Taisho University under Ryukai Mano. He served as a researcher at Taisho University (attested 1995–2006) and as an advisor to the Sravakabhumi Study Group until 2010.
Working in the fields of Buddhist studies and Indology, he studied under Kenyu Mitomo (attested 1996) and founded the Nikaya Buddhism Thought Study Group.

A scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology, he studied at the University of Tokyo under Tetsuro Watsuji (~1946–1949). He held posts at Yamanashi, Osaka, and Tsukuba universities, and became professor emeritus at J. F. Oberlin University (~1996–2005).

Specializing in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, he studied at Wako University (~1972–1976). He held professorial posts at Otemae University (~1987–1993), Nagoya University (~2003–2018), and Osaka University (attested 2004).

An Indologist and philosopher, he has held research associate positions at the University of Vienna (attested 2007), Leipzig University (attested 2015), and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (attested 2022).

A Buddhist studies scholar, he studied at Tohoku University. He held academic posts at Yamaguchi University and Koyasan University, and served as president of the Association of Esoteric Buddhist Studies (attested 2004).
A Buddhist studies scholar, she studied at Fo Guang University, earning an MA under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2009).
